Summary judgment is proper where there is no genuine dispute of material fact. Celotex Corp. v.
Catrett, 477 U.S. 317, 322 (1986). Separate-but-equal facilities satisfy equal protection. Plessy v.
Ferguson, 163 U.S. 537 (1896). The right recognized in Roe v. Wade, 410 U.S. 113 (1973), 93 S. Ct.
705, controls. Segregated schools were upheld. Smith v. Jones, 347 U.S. 483 (1954).
The Ninth Circuit agreed. Ramirez v. Pacific Freight Lines, 925 F.3d 1500 (9th Cir. 2019).
State courts have followed. People v. Alvarez, 14 Cal. 4th 155 (1996). The Court revisited the
question recently. Ohio v. EPA, 603 U.S. 279 (2024). Summary judgment standards also govern
the evidentiary burden. Anderson v. Liberty Lobby, Inc., 477 U.S. 242, 900 (1986).
